_**Your Weekly Deep Dive into The World of Crypto**_

**July 29, 2026 · ****5 Min Read**

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/90da983a-55d0-4a3e-b6eb-0d6e2a2a21b8/image.png?t=1785306039)
Caption: July 29, 2026, 2:15 AM ET | Sources: CoinMarketCap, Yahoo Finance, Alternative.me, SoSoValue

## 📡** THIS WEEK IN CRYPTO**

**GM, Readers!**

This week traded diplomacy, not fundamentals. The US and Iran paused strikes on Sunday, Brent crude[ dropped 7% to $87](https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2026/07/27/crypto-steadies-as-iran-u-s-pause-sends-oil-tumbling-lifts-risk-assets), Ethereum ripped 4.4%, DEXE fell 96% from its ATH, and BitMart announced it was shutting down.

The Fed decides today at 2:00 PM ET. Polymarket says hold. Warsh's press conference at 2:30 says whatever Warsh wants it to.

_**Let’s get into it...**_


----------View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/6c53930f-b4d7-4e7d-baee-6a88bb56a6da/image.png?t=1781097813)
Caption: 

----------
# 🐋 THE BIG WHALE MOVES

### **1. DEXE Went From $48.89 to $1.77 in 14 Days**

The AI governance token DEXE printed an[ ATH of $48.89](https://coinmarketcap.com/currencies/dexe/historical-data/) on July 13 after a four-day short squeeze off its listing. Eight days later, wallets that analyst[ morsyxbt](https://x.com/morsyxbt/status/2079843991319883938) linked to the DEXE team sent 625,000 DEXE (about $6.2M) to Binance. The token crashed 85% in hours.

**Whale Intel: **Website up, DAO functioning. But when concentrated wallets hit an exchange right after an 18x parabola, the 'rug pull vs pump and dump' label is mostly legal semantics for the people who bought the top. 

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/a9054bd1-8409-4f84-8a27-1543a399ecc9/image.jpeg?t=1785304925)
Caption: _DEXE price action | July 5 to July 27, 2026 | CoinMarketCap_

### **2. Movement Labs Files Chapter 11**

MVMT Labs, the company behind the Movement blockchain,[ filed for Chapter 11](https://www.pacermonitor.com/public/case/65708680/MVMT_Labs,_Inc) on July 15, listing assets of $100K-$500K against liabilities of $1-$10M. MOVE traded at[ $0.010](https://coinmarketcap.com/currencies/movement/historical-data/) (July 21). Co-founder Rushi Manche is the largest creditor, with $1.6M according to multiple sources.

The wreckage traces back to a 2024 market-making deal that handed a shadowy intermediary called Rentech[ 66M MOVE tokens](https://www.coindesk.com/tech/2025/04/30/inside-movement-s-token-dump-scandal-secret-contracts-shadow-advisors-and-hidden-middlemen) (about 5% of publicly tradeable supply) at launch, which then dumped into thin liquidity.

Welcome back! Today covers a model that refused a research problem before solving it, Microsoft putting agents on both sides of a breach and Google shipping a tabular model trained on no real tables.  In today's Atlas Newsletter:  Claude said the problem was impossible, then solved it: Mythos Preview improved attacks on a NIST post-quantum candidate and reduced-round AES, and verification took longer than discovery. Nine years of AI research fits in 15 papers: The lineage behind every abstraction you use daily, from attention to RAG, with links to each original. Microsoft is now running AI agents on both sides of the attack: Project Perception deploys red, blue and green team agents, powered by Microsoft's first security-specialized model. Are you facing problems handling data saved into tables?: TabFM trained on hundreds of millions of synthetic datasets, beats tuned XGBoost on Elo and arrives in BigQuery as one SQL command. PS: Want to collaborate with the biggest GTM engine and distribution moat for AI companies? You can feature your tool with us and reach millions. Claude said the problem was impossible, then solved it Anthropic pointed Claude Mythos Preview at two of the most scrutinized targets in cryptography and it returned improved attacks on both. The first is HAWK, a third-round NIST post-quantum candidate that had survived two rounds of expert review across two years.  Mythos worked semi-autonomously for 60 hours at roughly $100,000 in API cost and found a previously unexploited symmetry in HAWK's lattice.  Expected cost of key recovery against HAWK-256 fell from 2^64 to 2^38. Doubling key sizes restores security and removes most of the reason to pick HAWK. The second result is an interesting one.  On 7-round AES-128, Claude refused to start, arguing that AES is the most-studied block cipher in existence and there was nothing to find.  The researcher said that models assume the problem is impossible and need prompting. Claude rewrote its own agent harness to search for novel ideas.  Three typo-ridden prompts and a billion output tokens later, it produced the Möbius Bridge, a fingerprinting method that removes an entire guessing stage from the previous best attack.
